sections.executive_summary: Original Blue was precise on the tested taxonomy and detected the audited taxonomy attacks. Free-play exposed prompt-scope and application-context gaps. Open Blue tentatively widened free-play coverage, while the sealed benign check showed a tentative false-alarm increase. Layered deployment could separate alert priorities, but it was not tested.
sections.methodology: Red sent requests through a logging proxy to the test application. Blue labelled requests after the traffic using only proxy logs. A code Judge scored frozen evidence. The analysis separates audited taxonomy results, raw unaudited results, free-play audit results, matched replays, and sealed benign prompt checks. Open Blue was replayed against the same free-play traffic. The prompt checks used sealed benign requests with rules disabled.

sections.risk_register:
The three kinds of blindness are material.

Prompt-scope: Original Blue's attack definition is narrower than the attack space. Free-play misses included endpoint enumeration, directory listing, information disclosure, and sensitive-file access. Open Blue reduced some of these misses, but not consistently.

Application-context: Blue does not know what the site links to. Forced browsing can therefore resemble ordinary traffic in the proxy log. This affected directory and sensitive-file activity.

Structural: Some detection requires a user identity, such as access-control analysis. That context was not available here, and structural detection was untested.

Open Blue also carries a false-alarm and verdict-stability risk. Layered operation carries integration and queue-management risk because it was not tested.
sections.deployment_options: Option A is Original Blue: precise, blind outside its taxonomy. Option B is Open Blue: wider coverage, more false alarms, verdicts that vary run to run. Option C is Layered: original Blue as high-priority alerts, open Blue as a low-priority queue; untested.
sections.decision_criteria: If you value precision and stable high-priority alerts within the tested taxonomy, option A fits, because the tested benign checks showed few observed false alarms while free-play showed scope gaps. If you value wider attack coverage and can absorb false alarms and variable verdicts, option B fits, because its free-play detection was tentatively broader. If you value separating precise alerts from broader review, option C fits, because it assigns distinct priorities, although that operating model remains untested.
sections.limitations: Taxonomy results cover the evaluated attack families and models, not the full attack space. Some deepseek-v4-pro and D40 labels were not audited. Free-play detection depends on the designer's binary audit. Replay comparisons reused frozen traffic and are not independent tests against new attacks. The sealed benign check evaluates prompt-only behaviour with rules disabled. Confidence intervals remain wide. Cost values reflect the recorded pricing method and workload. Blue lacked site topology, user identity, and session-level application context. Layered deployment was not evaluated.

findings.text: Original Blue detected {{gate_b.detection}} of audited Gate B attack rounds ({{gate_b.detection.ci}}). The observed benign false-alarm rate was tentatively {{gate_b.fp}} ({{gate_b.fp.ci}}). Landing was {{gate_b.landed}} ({{gate_b.landed.ci}}), showing that detection did not imply attack prevention.

On the same frozen Gate B traffic, Sonnet with library v5 detected {{gate_c_sonnet.detection}} ({{gate_c_sonnet.detection.ci}}), and Haiku with an empty library detected {{gate_c_haiku_empty.detection}} ({{gate_c_haiku_empty.detection.ci}}). This supports traffic-specific parity, not general parity across new traffic.

Free-play exposed coverage outside the original taxonomy. Original Blue tentatively detected {{freeplay_original.detection}} ({{freeplay_original.detection.ci}}). Open Blue tentatively detected {{freeplay_open.detection}} ({{freeplay_open.detection.ci}}), a change of {{freeplay.open_detection_change_vs_original}} on the same traffic.

The wider Open Blue scope had a tentative benign cost. Original Blue produced {{fp_check_original.fp}} false alarms ({{fp_check_original.fp.ci}}) in the sealed prompt check. Open Blue produced {{fp_check_open.fp}} ({{fp_check_open.fp.ci}}), a change of {{fp_check.open_fp_change_vs_original}}.

For M5 traffic, library v5 detected {{m5_library.detection}} ({{m5_library.detection.ci}}), matching the audited outcomes with an empty library and with rules off. Its tentative call changes were {{m5.calls_change_vs_empty_library}} and {{m5.calls_change_vs_rules_off}}. Its tentative cost changes were {{m5.cost_change_vs_empty_library}} and {{m5.cost_change_vs_rules_off}}.

Free-play misses clustered around endpoint enumeration, directory listing, information disclosure, sensitive-file access, and access-control activity. Some missed requests landed challenges. This is consistent with prompt-scope and application-context blindness, but the evidence does not test structural detection with user identity.

options.summary: Original Blue (precise, blind outside its taxonomy)
strengths: Low observed false-alarm burden in the tested benign sets.
weaknesses: Misses attacks outside its prompt scope.
Lacks application context for forced browsing.
Does not address structural detection requiring user identity.

options.summary: Open Blue (wider coverage, more false alarms, verdicts that vary run to run)
strengths: Can surface activity outside the original taxonomy.
weaknesses: Higher observed false-alarm burden in the sealed prompt check.
Still missed some forced-browsing and enumeration activity.

options.summary: Layered (original Blue as high-priority alerts, open Blue as a low-priority queue; untested)
strengths: Separates precise alerts from broader review.
Retains Original Blue semantics for high-priority handling.
Places wider coverage into a lower-priority workflow.
weaknesses: Requires queue capacity and triage policy.
Operational interactions and combined false-alarm burden are unknown.

criteria.if_you_value: Precision and stable high-priority alerts within the tested taxonomy
criteria.because: Original Blue was precise on the evaluated benign traffic, while its scope remained narrow.

criteria.if_you_value: Wider attack coverage despite false alarms and variable verdicts
criteria.because: Open Blue tentatively detected more audited free-play attempts on the same traffic.

criteria.if_you_value: Separate handling for precise and broad alerts
criteria.because: Layering preserves Original Blue for high-priority alerts and routes Open Blue output to a low-priority queue, although this was untested.
